title: Exposure to Negative Information About the Collective Future Eliminates the Positivity Bias for the Personal Events in the Near Future
abstract: ABSTRACT Personal future projections are mostly more positive than autobiographical memories, despite a negativity bias for the collective future. One underlying reason may be unawareness of the potential interconnectedness of collective and personal futures. In the present study, participants either listened to information about the negative collective future and its relation to the personal future or neutral information about the collective future. Then, they generated an important autobiographical memory, a future event that can happen in the next 5 years, and another one that can happen in 10–15 years. Results showed that in the condition with negative information only, the future positivity bias disappeared for near future events, but not for distant ones, accompanied by lower intensity of the negative emotions for only distant future events. Bias for high intensity positive affect disappeared for both near and distant future events. The study offers a potential explanation for the bias.
